open_pull_requests.title: Stage 5D A–C: operator workspace and exact website publishing journey
open_pull_requests.body:
Implements the owner-approved Stage 5D **A–C only** under #398, including the requested competitive-pattern reassessment.

HiVenues previously made operators assemble publishing from internal Release and deployment screens. This PR carries one exact saved copy through content approval, destination consequence review, execution and the observed result. The follow-up study found that the first A–C workspace added overlapping navigation, so the editor now uses one tool hierarchy with site management in a named site menu.

### Competitive-pattern refinement
Official Wix/Wix Studio, Squarespace, Webflow, Shopify and Framer documentation informed a 15-row comparison. Direct interaction covered public Squarespace/Shopify template previews and Webflow's read-only preview workspace; Wix/Framer editing entry points stopped at sign-in. Authenticated competitor publishing was not claimed.

- Remove the permanent Edit website / Content / Website / History strip.
- Keep Page, Activities, Offers, Design and Settings as editor tools; place Website & hosting, History and Your places in the named site menu.
- Rename the generic Content form Story & visit details.
- Show honest unsaved/saving/saved/failure feedback; protect typed inspector and story-form edits from accidental navigation.
- Separate Design from participation/account settings.
- Use Desktop layout / Mobile layout and an honest local Save a copy action.
- Preserve explicit immutable approval, destination-specific confirmation and public read-back truth.

Matrix, sources, decisions and scope: [competitive-pattern study](docs/HIVENUES_STAGE5D_COMPETITIVE_PATTERNS.md). Original A–C notes: `docs/HIVENUES_ERA7_STAGE5D_AC_WORKSPACE_0_1_0.md`.

### A–C behavior
Server-derived operator presentation compares the draft and immutable copies with actual per-destination evidence. Preview retains draft/exact-copy identity. Content approval retains revision/digest guards and reuses identical content. Destination confirmation calls existing services and strict submission parsing. Installation success remains distinct from public HTTPS proof. Local-only and simulation states remain explicit.

### Safety and scope
No HostGraph, Release storage, deployment engine, authority, rollback restriction, stale-review, DNS/TLS validation, public evidence or restart-persistence semantics are replaced. No real provider, VPS, DNS, TLS, Hive, payment or other external mutation was performed.

Browser publishing exercises use a labelled offline fixture with the real installed service/coordinator and in-memory transport. They establish no live public proof. D–E connection/recovery and History redesign remain out of scope. The transient Studio client budget explicitly changes from <150 to <180 lines for unsaved-form protection; it holds no durable state, adds no autosave and no second island.

### Exact lineage
- Assessed #397 candidate: `e469282b39d533f1803dcd47b61663dbf05043de`
- Assessed tree: `9955d14e52114a091201118f7bc649e0153578ca`
- Prior A–C candidate / this refinement's parent: `a365d748f0f8d40dbf922fa9ffc7cd190248dee3`
- Current HEAD: `28eaf662df350e23ed02c25bde17bf78b311fa04`
- Current tree: `9e7dc9d616938d59d0a5735f88c7f26207d5ffc2`

The connected GitHub commit has the exact locally tested tree. Canonical commit bytes were verified and the local branch aligned without changing its working tree. This PR targets main; **#397 remains untouched and unmerged**. Integration remains an owner decision.

### Current local qualification
- Secret scan, lint and CSS build pass.
- 578 deterministic tests: **577 pass, 1 Windows-DPAPI-only skip, 0 fail**.
- Product browser: **101 screenshots/audits**, zero blocking accessibility findings, horizontal overflow, incomplete images, unauthorized controls, external requests or unexpected console errors.
- New behavioral checks cover discard cancellation, failed-save preservation and successful retry.
- Operator re-evaluation covers desktop and 320 px editing, unsaved-state feedback, mobile story editing, preview, History via site menu, local copy approval, and labelled offline destination confirmation/execution ending at **Public check pending**.
- Original independent first-use freeze remains unchanged across all 124 hashes.

The local browser manifest is marked LOCAL_UNBOUND because it ran before commit publication; the review evidence maps its unchanged source tree to the HEAD above. All seven applicable exact-HEAD workflows passed:

- [Era 5 runtime proof](https://github.com/etblink/HiVenues/actions/runs/37210047177): success
- [Era 5 signing preflight](https://github.com/etblink/HiVenues/actions/runs/37210047159): success
- [Product browser](https://github.com/etblink/HiVenues/actions/runs/37210047171): success
- [Era 5 clean-machine installer](https://github.com/etblink/HiVenues/actions/runs/37210047165): success
- [Public runtime bundle](https://github.com/etblink/HiVenues/actions/runs/37210047130): success
- [Era 5 Windows distributable](https://github.com/etblink/HiVenues/actions/runs/37210047127): success
- [CI](https://github.com/etblink/HiVenues/actions/runs/37210047133): success

Live Hive smoke and real external deployment were not requested. These qualifications do not establish a publicly deployed website.

**Stop for owner review. Do not merge #397, proceed to D–E, or declare #374 satisfied.**

open_pull_requests.title: Era 7 Stage 5C: make Release and deployment lifecycle legible
open_pull_requests.body:
Advances #396 and #374. No live infrastructure action is performed by this PR.

### Problem

The deployment machinery is now proven, but ordinary UI language still conflates:

```text
Working
Website Release
public deployment
domain / public verification
```

Real owner testing exposed several concrete ambiguities: **Currently Live** on Release review, **Publish website release**, stale **Bootstrap server...** wording on established deployments, and raw deployment state/provenance preceding ordinary intent.

### Stage 5C changes

- Release review now calls the immutable snapshot **Latest Website Release** and explicitly states that creating it does not update an external server/domain/DNS/TLS.
- **Create website Release** replaces the ambiguous publish button.
- Post-Release Studio feedback says an external deployment remains unchanged until the Release is put online.
- Urgent updates and restore review now use the same Release-vs-deployment distinction.
- Studio navigation names **Website Release** and **Put website online**.
- Deployment now leads with:
  ```text
  Working changes
  → Website Release
  → Put online
  → Connect domain
  → Verify public site
  ```
- Real deployment records receive a human-readable website status + next-step explanation before raw internals.
- IDs, raw state names, hashes and provider facts move under **Technical deployment details**.
- Offline synthetic and extra-target controls move under **Advanced and qualification targets**.
- Exact deployment review is lifecycle-aware:
  - first-server setup language on initial bootstrap;
  - ordinary update language on an established restricted target;
  - explicit runtime-maintenance language when the Website Release is unchanged.
- Raw consequence identifiers and exact target/Release/runtime provenance remain preserved under **Exact technical details**.

### Safety

No state-machine, deployment-package, authority, rollback, DNS/TLS, public-readback, Hive, provider-payment or fail-closed behavior is changed.

### Qualification

Adds deterministic Stage-5C regressions for:

- Release creation versus external deployment language;
- human deployment status before technical internals;
- established update review wording;
- first-server setup wording.

Existing browser qualification now explicitly opens the advanced qualification-target disclosure before exercising the synthetic target.

### Acceptance

Final usability acceptance remains with the project owner under #374. No fresh-human trial is required.

issue398.title: Era 7 Stage 5D — owner-facing visual and interaction redesign
issue398.body:
## Purpose

Respond to the failed owner acceptance under #374 by redesigning the ordinary HiVenues operator experience at the visual, information-architecture and interaction level.

Parent: #342  
Usability gate: #374  
Semantic/lifecycle foundation: #396 / PR #397

## Why this stage exists

Stage 5C improved lifecycle terminology, but direct owner use still produced the wrong mental model.

Observed from the qualified candidate:

- **Website Release** in the Studio header read as “publish my website.”
- The Release review page read as a historical-version chooser for selecting **Working**.
- When asked how to make the current version become what the real public domain serves, the owner chose **Create website Release** rather than Deployment.
- The owner reported that the screen could eventually be deciphered with significant reasoning, but did not feel intuitive.
- The current product therefore still requires the operator to mentally reconstruct internal state-machine concepts.

This is an interaction-design failure, not merely a copy defect.

## Governing principle

Preserve internally:

```text
Working
≠ immutable Website Release
≠ deployed Release
≠ verified public site
```

But do **not** require those nouns to dominate the ordinary workflow.

The user should understand what will happen from hierarchy, status, actions and consequence review before needing internal terminology.

## Design mandate

Reconsider the ordinary Studio and publication journey as a coherent product, including:

- top-level information architecture;
- primary and secondary actions;
- visual hierarchy;
- current-status presentation;
- “what am I editing / what is approved / what is online?” comprehension;
- the Release + deployment transition;
- update and rollback flows;
- history placement;
- progressive disclosure;
- empty/degraded/interrupted states;
- operator-friendly application lifecycle.

Do not merely restyle the current screens.

It is acceptable to propose a more human primary action such as **Publish changes** / **Update website** if the exact immutable Release + reviewed deployment steps remain preserved underneath and consequences are explicit.

## Visual quality bar

The Studio must feel like a serious 2026 creative product. The public-host-first design quality achieved elsewhere in HiVenues should not collapse into an administrative control panel when the operator manages the site.

Use the current owner screenshots as primary evidence.

## Astra role

Use GPT-6 Astra as a dedicated **Visual/Product Design Lead** for this stage.

### Working method: clone, run, use, then inspect

Astra should work from a real local checkout rather than from pasted snippets.

1. Clone `https://github.com/etblink/HiVenues.git` into a clean local workspace.
2. Record the exact starting `HEAD` and tree before making any changes.
3. Read #342, #374, #396, #398 and the governing product/doctrine documents.
4. Install the locked dependencies and launch HiVenues locally using the repository's supported development/runtime path.
5. **Before studying the relevant UI implementation in depth, use the running application through the browser as an ordinary HiVenues operator.**
   - Create/open a host.
   - Edit content.
   - Preview it.
   - Try to understand how to publish/update the real website.
   - Explore history, rollback, deployment, domain/public state, recovery and application quit/restart where available.
   - Record what the interface makes Astra believe will happen before clicking each consequential action.
6. Treat confusion, hesitation, wrong first guesses, excessive reading, visually buried actions, implementation vocabulary, and reliance on repository knowledge as product evidence.
7. Only after that operator-first pass, inspect the code as deeply as needed to understand why the UX behaves as it does and what can be safely changed.
8. Use the live app repeatedly while redesigning. Browser use is part of the design loop, not a final smoke test.

The repository is available for analysis and implementation, but Astra must not use source knowledge to excuse an interface that is unclear to an ordinary operator.

### First pass: diagnose and redesign before implementation

The first substantial pass should:

1. independently critique the existing end-to-end UX from the running product;
2. identify the mental model the current interface actually creates;
3. redesign the end-to-end interaction model;
4. produce concrete target screens / visual direction;
5. explicitly identify what should disappear from the ordinary path versus move behind progressive disclosure;
6. distinguish ordinary human tasks from internal state-machine nouns;
7. stop for owner review before committing to a broad implementation.

After the target interaction model is accepted, Astra may implement it in the same local clone in a separate bounded pass, continuously running and using the product in-browser while it works.

### Product-quality mandate

Astra is not being asked to “improve some screens.” It is responsible for making the supported HiVenues experience feel like a high-quality 2026 product.

It should optimize for:

- obvious next actions;
- low cognitive load;
- strong visual hierarchy;
- coherent navigation;
- confidence before consequential actions;
- clear distinctions between editing, publishing/updating the public site, history and recovery;
- beautiful, intentional creative-tool presentation;
- accessibility and responsive behavior;
- preservation of the exact safety/truth model underneath;
- minimal exposure of deployment/runtime terminology unless the operator asks for technical detail.

A successful result should make the owner think about their venue/site and desired action, not about HiVenues' internal architecture.

## Acceptance

Owner must be able to use the redesigned path from first instinct without being coached on the internal state machine.

The evaluation question is not “can the owner eventually reason it out?” but “does the product make the next safe action obvious?”

No fresh-human qualification is required; owner acceptance governs #374.

issue398_comments.body:
## Owner usability result — current A–C candidate rejected

The owner has now exercised the exact competitive-pattern candidate as a first-time-user simulation and reached the point where they would **exit HiVenues rather than continue**.

This is the decisive acceptance result for the current Stage 5D A–C implementation.

Observed failures during the owner walkthrough:

1. **First-run/home state is still ambiguous.** Fixture/example places appear under “Your places” and visually dominate the smaller “Create a place” action.
2. **Direct manipulation expectation is unmet.** The owner's first instinct in Studio was to click visible page content (for example the headline) to edit it. Visible content was not directly editable.
3. **Studio controls visually masquerade as host content.** Controls such as “Edit first impression”, “Edit activity”, “Edit content & visit facts”, image controls, etc. look like they belong to the visitor-facing design.
4. **Contextual editing loses object intent.** Clicking “Edit content & visit facts” beside visible menu/offering content opened a broad semantic form (identity, visit, story, invitation, etc.) rather than the content the owner expected to edit. The relationship between fields and rendered output was unclear.
5. **Editor/Preview fidelity failure.** The Studio canvas and Draft Preview are materially different compositions. The canvas showed duplicated offering/menu content that disappeared in Preview, and ordering/layout differed. The owner cannot confidently infer that editing the canvas means editing what visitors will actually see.
6. The cumulative result was not merely hesitation or excess reading. The owner stated that, as a first-time HiVenues user, **they would quit the program at this point**.

### Consequence

- Current A–C owner acceptance: **FAIL**
- PR #399 must remain draft/unmerged.
- Do not proceed to D–E.
- Do not declare #374 satisfied.
- Do not treat this as copy polish.

### Required redesign direction

The next pass should reconsider the editor around a familiar visual-builder interaction grammar:

- the **actual draft website** should be the primary editing surface;
- editor canvas and Preview must share the same composition/content hierarchy;
- selectable semantic objects should support direct manipulation where practical;
- hover/selection/editor affordances must be recognizably HiVenues chrome, not visitor content;
- clicking visible content should preserve object-level context into editing;
- broad semantic forms may remain for site/page facts, but must not substitute for contextual editing;
- first-run empty/onboarding state must be distinct from a returning-user “Your places” dashboard.

Preserve the exact Release/deployment/public-proof safety model underneath. The problem is the operator-facing authoring model.

Stop for redesign review before further broad implementation.

issue374.title: [Era 7 / Stage 5] Ordinary-operator lifecycle and usability convergence
issue374.body:
## Purpose

Preregister the **Era 7 Stage 5 ordinary-operator usability gate** now, while Stage 4 is beginning, so technical deployment success cannot later be mistaken for a finished human product.

Parent: #342  
Current active work: #372

## Governing requirement

> HiVenues is not complete merely because its deployment machinery works. An ordinary human must be able to understand and operate the supported lifecycle without Project Lead coaching, terminal knowledge, repository knowledge, or infrastructure vocabulary as a prerequisite.

The rigorous internal distinctions remain binding:

```text
Working
≠ Live
≠ immutable Release
≠ deployment
≠ server runtime
≠ domain/DNS/TLS
≠ provider/payment
```

But the ordinary UI must translate those truths into a comprehensible human workflow instead of requiring the operator to carry the internal state machine mentally.

## Target ordinary journey

The primary path should read approximately:

```text
Create
→ Design
→ Preview
→ Publish
→ Put it online
→ Connect domain
→ Confirm the public site
→ Make changes
→ Publish an update
→ Roll back when intentionally chosen
```

Advanced provenance, runtime identity, exact hashes, authority state and diagnostic detail remain available through progressive disclosure.

## Evidence motivating this gate

The Stage-3C real-server qualification successfully proved the machinery, but it also produced usability evidence:

- the operator repeatedly required exact coaching about which deployment action was safe;
- diagnostic/internal state language was prominent in ordinary screens;
- repair installs required knowing that closing the browser does not quit Studio;
- the operator had to terminate the product-owned background `node.exe` manually before repair-style installs;
- several safe recovery paths were technically present before they were obvious in the UI.

Those are valuable qualification findings, not reasons to weaken the underlying truth model.

## Required convergence

Before Era 7 may claim its ordinary-operator exit gate, qualify at least:

1. **Human vocabulary**
   - ordinary labels describe intent first;
   - implementation/provenance terminology is secondary detail.

2. **Progressive disclosure**
   - exact Release/runtime/DNS/TLS/authority evidence remains inspectable;
   - normal operation does not require understanding those internals.

3. **Clear primary action**
   - each normal state has an obvious next safe action;
   - dangerous or inapplicable actions are absent/disabled rather than requiring coaching.

4. **Coherent lifecycle**
   - Create → Edit → Preview → Publish → Deploy → Domain is legible as one product journey.

5. **Recovery UX**
   - degraded/interrupted state explains what happened and the safe recovery path;
   - no blind retry or manual server repair is required.

6. **Application lifecycle**
   - ordinary quit/restart behavior is explicit;
   - normal users are not expected to use Task Manager to understand whether Studio is still running.

7. **Useful empty states**
   - first-use and not-yet-configured states explain purpose and next action.

8. **Owner acceptance**
   - the project owner evaluates the supported Stage-5 lifecycle directly against the ordinary-operator standard;
   - approval is based on whether the product is understandable, coherent, and operable without developer-only knowledge being required by the product itself;
   - raw JSON/source editing, terminal work, repository knowledge, or Project Lead coaching remain usability defects if the product requires them for ordinary operation.

## Preserve

Usability convergence must not weaken:

- Working / Live / immutable Release truth;
- exact deployment/read-back proofs;
- fail-closed safety boundaries;
- non-custodial Hive authority;
- deployment credential separation;
- accessibility;
- restart persistence;
- provider-neutral architecture.

The goal is to **hide complexity without hiding consequences**.

## Timing

This issue is preregistration only while Stage 4 is active.

Do not divert #372 into a broad Studio redesign. Stage 4 should finish the truthful domain/DNS/TLS/public-read-back machinery first. Stage 5 then qualifies the complete installed-product lifecycle and performs the explicit usability convergence required by this issue.

## Exit

Stage 5 cannot close until the project owner explicitly approves the supported end-to-end lifecycle as meeting the ordinary-operator usability standard, while all exact internal truth/evidence remains preserved.

## Usability evidence from first real Stage-5 operator lifecycle

After the operator clicked **Publish website release** to create Release B, the same screen immediately showed:

- Working Version 3;
- Currently Live Version 3;
- "No visitor-facing difference was detected from the current live website."

This is semantically correct inside Studio because the new local Release has already become Studio's Live snapshot, but it is easy for a human operator to read **Currently Live** / **Publish website release** as meaning the Internet deployment at dev.fourthstreetbar.com was updated.

In the actual deployment model, the public VPS remains on the previously confirmed immutable Release until a separate Deployment package/review/consequence occurs.

Treat this as concrete ordinary-human UX evidence: Release/Studio-Live versus deployed-public state needs clearer language and transition feedback in the later usability pass.

issue374_comments.body:
## Owner acceptance result — NOT ACCEPTED

The project owner directly exercised the qualified Stage-5C candidate and rejected the current user-facing experience as meeting the ordinary-operator standard.

Observed owner mental model from the actual product:

1. **Working** was interpreted as the pending candidate for release.
2. From the Studio header, **Website Release** was interpreted as the way to publish the website.
3. On the Website Release review page, the owner interpreted the page as choosing which historical version should become **Working**.
4. When asked how to make the current version what `dev.fourthstreetbar.com` serves, the owner still chose **Create website Release** rather than **Open Deployment**.
5. The owner's conclusion: the page can be deciphered with significant reasoning, but it is not intuitive; the user-facing portion needs major improvement.

This is a substantive Stage-5 usability failure, not a wording nit.

The underlying state model remains valuable and must be preserved, but the present information architecture, visual hierarchy, action hierarchy and operator vocabulary still expose too much internal implementation structure.

Therefore:

- #374 remains OPEN;
- owner acceptance is NOT granted;
- PR #397 must remain UNMERGED as an acceptance candidate;
- the next pass should be treated as a visual/product interaction redesign, not another local copy-edit cycle;
- exact Working / immutable Release / deployment / public-proof semantics remain non-negotiable internally, but the ordinary operator should not have to reconstruct that state machine mentally.

The redesign should be validated again from first instinct, not by explaining the intended model before the owner uses it.
